_meta.source: docs/CONTENT.md draft 2 (Goods, New), docs/tech/balance.md stat sheet
_meta.status: staging input for the catalogue importer; written by an AI, not yet reviewed by the owner
_meta.keyed_by: The good's English name exactly as CONTENT.md lists it.

vanilla_loc_pattern.comment_column: Vanilla puts a short note for translators in the third CSV column. 'translator_comment' is that note.

suggested_mod_key_pattern.note: <Id> is the 'id' field without its Pandaborn prefix.

field_rules.singular / plural: Sentence case, as vanilla writes goods ('Maple pastry', 'Treated planks'). Mass nouns use the same word for both ('Bread', 'Wheat flour'). Goods that only make sense in the plural use the plural for both ('Berries', 'Coffee beans').
field_rules.eaten_raw: true means the game shows the vanilla line Goods.EatableRaw ('Can be eaten raw.') by itself. Nothing to write.
field_rules.tooltip: One optional line saying where the good comes from and what it is for. Vanilla goods carry no description, so this has no vanilla key. Use it only if the mod adds its own good tooltip or a crop or recipe hint (suggested key Pandaborn.Good.<Id>.Tooltip).

_meta.vanilla_goods_reused: Logs, gears, paper, scrap metal, metal blocks, water, berries, badwater, explosives, fireworks, dirt and antidote keep their vanilla keys and text.
_meta.pole_rename_warning: If a pole is the vanilla Plank shown under a faction-only name, the strings below must be shown through a faction-scoped key. Writing them to Good.Plank.DisplayName would rename planks for Folktails and Iron Teeth as well.

Bamboo shoots.tooltip: The village's first crop. Eat them raw, or steam them to feed twice as many.
Bamboo shoots.translator_comment: The young edible shoot of a bamboo plant. The Inkpaws' starter food, like the carrot.

Poles.tooltip: Cut from timber bamboo. No mill needed. The Inkpaws build with poles where others use planks.
Poles.translator_comment: A cut length of bamboo used as building material. It plays the part of the Plank.

Cured poles.tooltip: Poles hardened over smoke in the Smoke Kiln. Used for late construction.
Cured poles.translator_comment: A bamboo pole hardened by smoke. It plays the part of the Treated plank. Use the same word for pole as in Pole.

Cabbage.tooltip: A sturdy second crop. Eat it raw, pickle it, or put it in hot pot.
Cabbage.translator_comment: Chinese cabbage (napa cabbage), a leafy vegetable. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Rice.tooltip: Grown in flooded paddies. Steam it, or pound it into rice flour.
Rice.translator_comment: Harvested rice grain, not yet cooked.

Rice flour.tooltip: Rice pounded in the Trip-Hammer Mill. Used for sweet rice balls and bamboo seed cakes.
Rice flour.translator_comment: Flour made from rice. Use the same word for rice as in Rice.

Steamed shoots.tooltip: Bamboo shoots from the Steamer. The first cooked dish.
Steamed shoots.translator_comment: Steamed bamboo shoots, a simple cooked dish. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Steamed rice.tooltip: Rice from the Steamer. A staple meal.
Steamed rice.translator_comment: Plain cooked rice. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Pickles.tooltip: Cabbage pickled in the Pickle Yard. One cabbage makes several.
Pickles.translator_comment: Sichuan-style pickled cabbage kept in clay jars. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Sweet rice balls.tooltip: Soft rice-flour balls with a persimmon filling. The festival sweet.
Sweet rice balls.translator_comment: Tangyuan: soft round balls of rice-flour dough with a sweet filling, eaten at the Lantern Festival. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating them.

Sichuan pepper.tooltip: A spice from dry ground. Not a food on its own. Used for hot pot.
Sichuan pepper.translator_comment: The numbing spice (the husks of Zanthoxylum berries), not chili and not black pepper.

Hot pot.tooltip: Cabbage, Sichuan pepper and bamboo mushrooms in one pot. The best everyday meal.
Hot pot.translator_comment: Sichuan hot pot: a shared pot of spiced broth in which food is cooked at the table. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Tea leaves.tooltip: Picked from tea bushes on dry ground. Roasted and brewed into tea.
Tea leaves.translator_comment: Fresh leaves picked from a tea bush, before roasting.

Tea.tooltip: A drink with its own need. It also quenches some thirst: one measure of water makes three cups.
Tea.translator_comment: Brewed tea, a drink. Also the name of the need satisfied by drinking it.

Persimmons.tooltip: Picked from persimmon trees. A snack, and the filling of sweet rice balls.
Persimmons.translator_comment: The orange fruit of the persimmon tree (Diospyros kaki). Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Bamboo mushrooms.tooltip: A delicacy gathered in standing groves of timber bamboo. Used for hot pot.
Bamboo mushrooms.translator_comment: Bamboo fungus ('zhusun' in Chinese), a lacy white delicacy that grows in bamboo groves. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating it.

Bamboo seed.tooltip: Dropped once by bamboo that has flowered. Used for bamboo seed cakes.
Bamboo seed.translator_comment: The grain-like seed that bamboo drops after its rare mass flowering. A mass noun, like 'grain'.

Bamboo seed cakes.tooltip: Made from bamboo seed and rice flour. The best food the village knows, and only possible after a Great Flowering.
Bamboo seed cakes.translator_comment: Cakes made from bamboo seed. Use the same words as in Bamboo seed. Also the name of the need satisfied by eating them.

Paper lanterns.tooltip: Made in the Lantern Workshop for the Lantern Festival and for decoration.
Paper lanterns.translator_comment: A lantern of paper on a bamboo frame, the festival good.

recipe_names._note: Vanilla names a recipe only when one good can be made in more than one way (Manufactory.Recipe.<Id>, for example 'Biofuel (Carrots)'). Otherwise the recipe shows the product's name. No Inkpaw recipe needs its own name today. If steamed dishes ever share a product, follow the vanilla form: 'Product (Ingredient)'.
